q: To whom did Paul write his short letter named Philemon?
quote: To Philemon our beloved fellow worker

q: In Philemon, for whom does Paul make his appeal?
quote: I appeal to you for my child Onesimus

q: In Philemon, Paul asks Philemon to receive Onesimus as a beloved what?
quote: no longer as a slave, but better than a slave, as a beloved brother.

q: In Philemon, Onesimus was once useless but has now become what?
quote: Formerly he was useless to you, but now he has become useful both to you and to me.

q: In Philemon, what did Paul say to do with anything Onesimus owed?
quote: But if he has wronged you in any way or owes you anything, charge it to my account.

q: In Philemon, how does Paul describe himself?
quote: Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus

q: In Philemon, what did Paul ask Philemon to prepare for him?
quote: In the meantime, prepare a guest room for me

q: In Philemon, whom does Paul call our fellow soldier?
why: He was part of the house church.
